sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ready to learn **Introduction to Objects and Classes**?

Here's what we'll cover:

• Overview of object-oriented programming
• Why this matters for your coding journey
• Hands-on examples you can try

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Think of **Introduction to Objects and Classes** like building blocks. 

Every great program starts with small, simple pieces. This is one of those essential pieces!

• Start simple, then build up
• Practice makes it click
• Don't worry if it takes time - totally normal!

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: A class is a blueprint that defines the data fields and methods for objects
An object is a specific instance of a class created with the new keyword
Object-oriented programming organizes code around objects rather than functions
Encapsulation bundles data and methods that operate on that data into a single unit
OOP models real-world entities as objects with state (fields) and behavior (methods)

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Introduction to Objects and Classes - Overview of object-oriented programming. Master basics before advancing. Practice with the examples. Builds foundation for what's next.

questions.question: What is a class in object-oriented programming?
options: A blueprint or template for creating objects
questions.explanation: A class is a blueprint or template that defines the properties (data fields) and behaviors (methods) that objects created from it will have.

questions.question: What is an object?
options: An instance of a class with its own data values
questions.explanation: An object is a specific instance of a class. It has its own set of data field values defined by the class blueprint. For example, different Circle objects can have different radii.
